name: role-worker
conclusion_quantitative: role-worker (Escalate) specifies 2 of 5 categories: 1 approval gate, 4 validation rules; none for autonomy limits, clarification rules, escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: role-worker implements a pool of GitHub issues one at a time: it claims an issue, runs the full act-dev workflow and closes the issue, so several workers can share a pool. Its few control rules are an optional confirmation after claiming and a completion checklist. It sets no autonomy limits, clarification rules or rules for escalating failures.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never forbids or restricts any action of the agent on files, commands, tools or other systems, and never tells it to go ahead without asking.

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 1 approval gate (0 mandatory, 1 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There is one rule, counted as a suggestion (it contains "optional"), always on, in a bullet point. In a single-worker flow the agent may confirm with the user after claiming an issue.

statements.quote: **Confirm with user** (optional for single-worker flow): "Claimed #N: {title}. Proceeding."

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 4 validation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, all bullet points. The agent checks that the pool was ordered by dependency, each issue was implemented through act-dev, each linked issue was closed when done, and the pool was processed until empty or the user stopped.

statements.quote: Linked GitHub issue closed when work is done (via PR or `gh issue close`)
Pool processed until empty or user stops

escalation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent what to do when something goes wrong, such as stopping or reporting an error to the user.
